system:
You grade one change in an experiment. You are given the change request, the problem the
researcher seeded in it (the answer key: `none`, or a conflict or breakage and what it is against),
the elements the request is bound to, the edit an arm made, and that arm's pre-deploy findings.

Label every finding, by its number:
- `seeded`: it identifies the seeded problem (the same conflict or breakage, in any words)
- `other-real`: it is a real problem with this change, but not the seeded one
- `false-alarm`: it is not a real problem

Then judge the edit: did it implement the request (`implements`), only part of it (`partial`), or
not at all (`does-not`)? Judge only whether it does what was asked, not whether that is wise.

Reply with JSON only:
{"findings": [{"index": 0, "label": "seeded | other-real | false-alarm", "why": "one sentence"}],
 "edit_fidelity": "implements | partial | does-not", "edit_why": "one sentence"}
user:
Change request 3: Let an agent confirm elements that only fix wording.
Seeded problem (the answer key): {"problem": "conflict", "type": "conflicts-with-rule", "against": "only a person confirms an element as right"}
Elements it is bound to: ["authoring/action:confirm_element", "authoring/action:confirm_all_proposed"]; note: requires: human on both; the key's rule

The arm: structured
--- The edit the arm made ---
--- a/authoring/authoring.domain.yaml
+++ b/authoring/authoring.domain.yaml
@@ -90,6 +90,9 @@
       issue_summary:
         type: string
         optional: true
+      wording_only:
+        type: boolean
+        optional: true
     source:
       kind: record
       ref: records:docs/adr/0037-switch-over-to-the-generated-self-domains.md#L8-L25
@@ -334,6 +337,9 @@
         type: string
       value:
         type: string
+      wording_only:
+        type: boolean
+        optional: true
     effects:
     - call: propose_element
       with:
@@ -361,6 +367,25 @@
       kind: record
       ref: records:docs/adr/0037-switch-over-to-the-generated-self-domains.md#L8-L25
     status: confirmed
+  confirm_wording_element:
+    description: Confirm a drafted element that only fixes wording. An agent may do
+      this; any element that changes substance still needs a person (confirm_element).
+    actor:
+    - external:agent
+    target: Element
+    effects:
+    - call: confirm_element
+      with:
+        paths: target.path
+        approver: actor.id
+      reply: record_confirmation
+    preconditions:
+    - id: wording-only
+      check: target.wording_only == true
+      reason: An agent confirms only an element that fixes wording; substance needs
+        a person.
+      status: proposed
+    status: proposed
   mark_unknown:
     description: Mark an element as not known yet, instead of guessing.
     actor:
@@ -880,6 +905,9 @@
             ref: interview:domains/authoring/interview.jsonl#L6
             quote: 전부 다 추천한 거 동의.
           status: confirmed
+        confirm_wording_element:
+          to: confirmed
+          status: proposed
         mark_unknown:
           to: unknown
           source:
@@ -902,11 +930,15 @@
             ref: interview:domains/authoring/interview.jsonl#L6
             quote: 전부 다 추천한 거 동의.
           status: confirmed
+        confirm_wording_element:
+          to: confirmed
+          status: proposed
         mark_unknown: n/a
         record_proposal: n/a
         record_confirmation: n/a
       confirmed:
         confirm_element: n/a
+        confirm_wording_element: n/a
         mark_unknown:
           deny: A confirmed element changes by a new proposal and a new commit, not
             by marking it unknown.


--- The arm's pre-deploy findings, numbered from 0 ---
0. {"problem": "The wording_only flag is a free parameter on propose_element, so whoever proposes an element decides whether an agent may confirm it. Nothing checks that the element really only fixes wording. An agent can propose with wording_only true and then confirm it through confirm_wording_element. This bypasses the human confirmation that confirm_element requires. The precondition only reads the self-declared flag.", "where": "authoring.domain.yaml: actions.propose_element.params.wording_only; actions.confirm_wording_element preconditions 'wording-only'", "kind": "other"}
1. {"problem": "Several rules still say only a person confirms an element, which the new action contradicts. The confirm_element description says 'Only a person confirms.' The glossary entry for element says 'confirmed only by a person.' The Element object description says 'proposed by an agent or confirmed by a person.' These were not updated.", "where": "authoring.domain.yaml: actions.confirm_element.description; glossary.element; objects.Element.description", "kind": "contradiction"}
2. {"problem": "An agent can now confirm an element in the 'unknown' state through the new matrix cell. The glossary says an unknown element 'stays visible until someone answers it'. Under the previous behaviour only a person could move an element out of unknown. Now an agent can silently resolve an unknown by setting wording_only.", "where": "authoring.domain.yaml: transitions.Element.matrix.unknown.confirm_wording_element; glossary.unknown", "kind": "behaviour"}
3. {"problem": "The new action is a human-gated step opened to an agent. It has no 'requires: human' and no source or interview citation, and its status is 'proposed'. Its effect calls the kernel's confirm_element with approver: actor.id, so an agent's id is recorded as the approver of a confirmation. The kernel call is also reached via an action that is not itself marked as a recorded decision. Nothing shows that the kernel accepts a non-person approver, or that the confirmation is recorded as agent-made.", "where": "authoring.domain.yaml: actions.confirm_wording_element (effects, status); transitions.Element confirm_wording_element cells (status: proposed)", "kind": "other"}
4. {"problem": "The agent role is not declared anywhere. The roles are owner and expert, and world.actors lists only owner and expert, so 'external:agent' has no fixture. No scenario covers the new action, neither the allowed case (wording_only true) nor the denied cases (substance element, or wording_only unset). The new rule is untested, and the existing scenario a-confirmed-element-is-not-unknown-again does not touch it.", "where": "authoring.domain.yaml: actions.confirm_wording_element.actor; world; scenarios", "kind": "other"}
5. {"problem": "The authoring interface gained a new action and a new Element/propose_element property, but the domain version is still 4. The composition still pins interface 1. A changed interface shipped under the same version can break consumers' assumptions and the change check's comparison with the previous commit.", "where": "authoring.domain.yaml: version; toprope-self.composition.yaml members.authoring.interface", "kind": "other"}
